title: No king without a nation: Malchus, hisnasus and the reason for the tzimtzum
overview:
Chapter 48 begins the details of the building of *Malchus*, the bride who includes everything: in speech every level, from the essential will of the *Ein Sof* down to *Zeir Anpin*, comes out as a separate something. The class opens by finishing chapter 47: *Malchus* is a code, which can be copied over without knowing what it means, like a message memorized in a language one does not know, and the Torah is the source code of the world.

Then the chapter's point. The word of the king is *hisnasus*, rising above. *Chesed* is in a man even with no one to be kind to; *hisnasus* is built only from others, so a speaker stops when the listener falls asleep, and a comedian will not play to an empty hall. Still, it is hidden in a person from birth, a baby wants to rule the animals, and it is what sets man apart from the animals. There is no king without a nation, so over whom could G-d rule? He had to think up somebody else: that is why there is a *tzimtzum*, a *makom panui*, and a *masach* below *Atzilus*, and why *Malchus* is renewed every *Rosh Hashana*.

terms.gloss: a bride; Malchus, kelula (included) of everything, because all the sefiros are in speech
the building of an attribute: what it is actually built from, as against what only rouses it
back to back: Malchus before the nesira as a whole partzuf looking backwards, more than a mere tail
a tail: the lowest way Malchus is included in Zeir Anpin before the nesira
the word of the king: speech, the real kingdom of the king, to say what to do
rising above; the attribute of Malchus, built only from someone else to rise over
another, someone besides oneself; Malchus has no existence without one
a man of kindness: kindness is in him even with no one to do good to
I shall rule: the thought in the Essence before the tzimtzum, drawn down anew every Rosh Hashana
the empty place of the first tzimtzum, made so that there be something outside the Essence to rule over
glory, showing off: only before a stranger, yet the wish for it comes from oneself

sections.title: Malchus, the bride: speech makes everything a separate thing
sections.summary: *Malchus* is called *kalla* because it includes everything: in speech every level, from the essential will of the *Ein Sof* down to *Zeir Anpin*, comes out as a separate something, and it is equal in *Malchus* of the *Ein Sof* and *Malchus* of *Atzilus*.

phrases.he: (מח) והנה בחינת פרטות הבנין דמלכות הנקרא כלה
שכלולה מהכל כו',
phrases.en: because the *Malchus* has from all the *sefiros* in it

phrases.he: היינו מה שבבחינת הדבור מתגלה הכל בבחינת יש ודבר נבדל, כאותיות הדבור שמגלה הכל

blocks.title: A message memorized in a language he doesn't know
blocks.text: A computer seems to give over the whole connection, and you say, "Wow, what a smart computer!" But all it does is copy the shapes of the sounds, piece by piece, into a digital code, white black black white, the same as the telephone does. It is like a coded message passed from one man to the next, or a man who memorizes a message in a language he does not know, sound by sound, so that he says it exactly right to the man on the other side with no idea what he is saying. Like people who sing English songs, with the Western accent and the whole bit, and don't know what they're saying.
blocks.outOfPlace: Tape 227 opens by finishing the teaching of chapter 47 on Malchus as a separate thing that can be copied, then goes over chapter 47 quickly, before it reads the first line; placed under the first line, which picks up the same subject.

blocks.text: This is one of the *inyanim* (matters) of *Malchus* (kingship), *davka* (specifically) in *Malchus*. *Chachma* (wisdom) and *bina* (understanding) you cannot transmit unless you actually have them; nor emotion, which cannot go into the voice unless it is in the heart: even actors have to hype themselves up into having it. But once it is in *Malchus*, it is a *davar yesh nifrad* (a separate something), which can be copied from place to place without knowing what it is. That is how *Atik* gets copied over from *Malchus* of the *Ein Sof*.
blocks.outOfPlace: Tape 227 opens by finishing the teaching of chapter 47 on Malchus as a separate thing that can be copied, then goes over chapter 47 quickly, before it reads the first line; placed under the first line, which picks up the same subject.

blocks.title: Copying a page in Russian
blocks.text: A person can sit down and copy a page in Russian, or in French, letter for letter, without understanding a word of it, and make a copy for somebody. The meaning still goes over; it makes no difference that he does not know what it says. The meaning is already coded in. That is the whole thing: the encoding.
blocks.outOfPlace: Tape 227 opens by finishing the teaching of chapter 47 on Malchus as a separate thing that can be copied, then goes over chapter 47 quickly, before it reads the first line; placed under the first line, which picks up the same subject.

blocks.title: The Torah codes
blocks.text: That reminds him of an email about the Torah codes that he never answered. What they are coming up with is the very tip of the iceberg; they have no idea. The Torah is literally the codes. It is not just that the name of Saddam Hussein is hidden in its letters: there is a Saddam Hussein because his encoding is in the Torah. Without it there could be no DNA of Saddam Hussein, and he could not have been born. There is such a thing as gold because the encoding of that element is in the Torah. It is much deeper than they think.
blocks.outOfPlace: Tape 227 opens by finishing the teaching of chapter 47 on Malchus as a separate thing that can be copied, then goes over chapter 47 quickly, before it reads the first line; placed under the first line, which picks up the same subject.

blocks.title: Pac-Man and the source code
blocks.text: They call the Torah the blueprint of the universe. It is more than a blueprint: it is the source, the source code. You can play Pac-Man only if the code is fed into the computer; those little guys run around the screen trying to eat you up because the source code is there making it happen. The Torah is literally the source code of the world. Its letters keep the world in existence: it is the program. That He looked into the Torah and created the world is like a computer that reads the source code, follows the directions and passes them on to its peripherals, and that is how all the people run around on your screen.
blocks.outOfPlace: Tape 227 opens by finishing the teaching of chapter 47 on Malchus as a separate thing that can be copied, then goes over chapter 47 quickly, before it reads the first line; placed under the first line, which picks up the same subject.

blocks.text: A recording of seminars downloaded onto a computer holds no voice at all, only a code, finally a binary code, 1 0 0 1. The computer reads it, and the code tells it: now make this sound. Once a thing is in a code, the code can be transferred without knowing what it means, and it is *davka Malchus* that can do that. That is the whole *inyan* of *Malchus*: it is the code of a thing, which makes it into a separate somethingness.
blocks.outOfPlace: Tape 227 opens by finishing the teaching of chapter 47 on Malchus as a separate thing that can be copied, then goes over chapter 47 quickly, before it reads the first line; placed under the first line, which picks up the same subject.

blocks.text: Going over chapter 47: the speech, the *maamar* (saying) "Let there be light, and there was light", is a *davar nivdal* (a separate thing) by itself. *Malchus* of *chesed* (kindness) becomes *chesed* of *Malchus*, and even *Malchus* of *chachma* of *chesed* becomes *chachma* of *chesed* of *Malchus*: the *sefiros* of the *sefiros*. He mentions three states before the *nesira* (the sawing apart): *achor b'achor* (back to back), *achor b'panim* and a *zanav* (tail). They are different ways *Malchus* is included in *Zeir Anpin*: a *zanav* is only a tail; *achor b'achor* is a whole *partzuf* looking backwards; higher still is the inner *Malchus*, the letters the *chesed* comes from in the first place. First she is a *nekuda* (point) under *yesod*: she fell under his feet.
blocks.outOfPlace: Tape 227 opens by finishing the teaching of chapter 47 on Malchus as a separate thing that can be copied, then goes over chapter 47 quickly, before it reads the first line; placed under the first line, which picks up the same subject.

blocks.text: Then the two buildings of *Malchus*: the *binyan* (building) of *Malchus*, the building of the speech itself, like the *mashal*; and *Malchus* of *Malchus*, building how it will come out exactly, in letters. *Chachma* and *bina* built her and told her, "Go out to be a head to the foxes." The *dibur sheb'machshava* (speech within thought) became *machshava sheb'dibur* (thought within speech), the *dalet* of *dvar melech shilton*, called *dalet* because it is *Tanhi* (*tiferes*, *netzach*, *hod* and *yesod*): the *Tanhi* of *Zeir Anpin* is dressed in the speech.
blocks.outOfPlace: Tape 227 opens by finishing the teaching of chapter 47 on Malchus as a separate thing that can be copied, then goes over chapter 47 quickly, before it reads the first line; placed under the first line, which picks up the same subject.

blocks.text: There is a *Malchus* before the speech itself, *Keser Malchus*; then the ten *sefiros* of *Malchus*; then the *Malchus* of *Malchus* that comes through. After *Moshiach* comes they will be equal in stature again, as before: in a way *Malchus* preceded the *middos*. Like the moon, it grows less and more. *Atzilus* is called a day and *Beriya, Yetzira and Asiya* a night. That is going over the chapter real fast, just to remember it good.
blocks.outOfPlace: Tape 227 opens by finishing the teaching of chapter 47 on Malchus as a separate thing that can be copied, then goes over chapter 47 quickly, before it reads the first line; placed under the first line, which picks up the same subject.

blocks.text: Now the details of the building of *Malchus*, called *kalla* (bride) because she is *kelula* (included) of everything: **the *Malchus* has from all the *sefiros* in it**. In speech everything is revealed as a *yesh* (something), a separate thing: in speech you can have the emotions, the intellect and the *ratzon* (will) too.

phrases.he: והוא גם מבחינת התענוג ורצון העצמי שבעצמות אור אין סוף ממש, בבחינת חפץ חסד ההיולי הנזכר (באות הי') כשבא בהשתלשלות רבות עד רצון וחכמה ומדות דאדם קדמון ואריך אנפין עד בחינת רצון וחכמה ומדות חיצוניות הכלים דזעיר אנפין, הכל בא בבחינת המלכות, בחינת הדבור העליון, בהתגלות יש בבחינת האצילות
שעל זה אמר אני ראשון ואני אחרון,
phrases.en: I'm at the beginning, I'm at the end

phrases.he: וכן ראו כי אני אני הוא,
בחינת מלכות דאין סוף במלכות דאצילות, סופא דכל דרגין כו'

blocks.text: All the levels, from the essential will of the *Ein Sof* down to *Zeir Anpin*, come in *Malchus*: **I'm at the beginning, I'm at the end**. As a person's whole self comes out in his speech, so upstairs in *Malchus* of *Atzilus*. **I am the same one**: *Malchus* of the *Ein Sof* and of *Atzilus* are equal on every level. Everything, even the essence of the will, comes into the speech.

sections.title: Malchus is built anew every Rosh Hashana, and the king's word is hisnasus
sections.summary: The *Keser* of *Malchus* is built on *Rosh Hashana*, drawing down anew the will to reign, *Ana Emloch*. The revelation in speech is the word of the king, and it is the attribute of *hisnasus*, rising above.

phrases.he: ותחלה יש להבין דרך פרט בפרצוף המלכות, מבחינת כתר שבה עד בחינת המלכות שבה שבוקע המסך להיות כתר לבריאה כו' דהנה בראש השנה הוא בנין כתר הנוקבא כו', והוא מה שאומרים י' פסוקים מלכיות כו' דהיינו להמשיך בחינת התענוג והרצון למלוכה מחדש, שהוא לעורר מחדש בחינת התענוג והרצון הפשוט שבעצמות, להיות אנא אמלוך כו' (והיינו ענין גבורי כח עושי דברו כו' הנזכר בזהר, כמו שכתוב במקום אחר בענין ויתנו לך כתר מלוכה כו')

blocks.text: First the *partzuf* (stature) of *Malchus* is to be understood in detail, from its *Keser* (crown) to its *Malchus*, which breaks through the *masach* (screen) to be the *Keser* of *Beriya*. On *Rosh Hashana* the *Keser* of the *nukva* (the female, *Malchus*) is built, and the ten verses of *malchiyos* (kingship) are said: to draw down anew the delight and the will to reign, *Ana Emloch* (I shall rule). That is when the *binyan hamalchus* comes out, on *Rosh Hashana*.

phrases.he: בהיות ידוע שבחינת ההתגלות בדבור הנזכר לעיל, הוא הנקרא דבר מלך,
phrases.en: *davka* the speech is the real kingdom of the king, to say what to do

phrases.he: והוא בחינת מדת ההתנשאות, כמו שכתוב יהו״ה מלך גאות כו' וכן מלכותך מלכות כו'

blocks.text: The revelation in speech is called *dvar melech*, the word of the king: **the speech is the real kingdom of the king, to say what to do**. It is *hisnasus* (rising above), as it says, *Hashem malach gei'us*: *Malchus sheb'Malchus*.

sections.title: Hisnasus is built from someone else; chesed is not
sections.summary: Kindness is in a man even with no one to be kind to; rising above exists only over another, and grows or shrinks with how much the others defer to him, as a speaker stops when no one listens.

phrases.he: וכמו על דרך משל מדת ההתנשאות באדם, שהוא בחינת מדה נבדלת מן העצמות, להיות מתנשא על זולתו דוקא כו', מה שאין כן שאר המדות שהן חלק ממש מן העצמות כמו אור מדת החסד, שהנפש עצמה נמשכת ומתפעלת מהחסד, כי עיקר מדה זו המשכה מן העצמות הוא, כמו כן החכמה נמשכת מן העצם כו' אבל מדת ההתנשאות, הגם שהנפש מתפעלת ממנה, אבל העיקר שלה הוא המתהווה מן הדבר הנבדל מן העצם, שהוא על זולתו, ואם אין דבר זולתו לא תתעורר מדה זו כלל
והגם שבחינת החסד גם כן להטיב חסדו לזולתו דוקא, אבל מכל מקום תחלת התהוותה הוא בעצמותו, גם שאין איש להטיב עמו,
phrases.en: The thing of the *chesed*, even though it's *davka* to somebody else, but nonetheless, the thing that he is, he's *chesed*, he himself is an *ish chesed*

phrases.he: מה שאין כן בהתנשאות, שלא תתהווה בעצם מציאותה בלתי מי שיש להתנשאות עליו

blocks.text: The lines are read without comment. *Hisnasus* in a person is an attribute separate from the self, to rise *davka* over someone else, unlike the other *middos* (attributes), which are an actual part of the self: the soul is drawn into *chesed* whether it wants to or not, and *chachma* too is drawn from the self. *Hisnasus* moves the soul as well, but it comes into being from the thing apart from the self; with no one else, it is not roused at all.

*Chesed* too is *davka* doing good to another, yet it starts in the self even with no one to do good to: **he himself is an *ish chesed***. *Hisnasus* cannot come into being without someone to rise over.

phrases.he: וראיה לזה ממה שכל עיקר בנינה בהתפשטות אורך ורוחב תלוי רק בביטול האנשים, כשירוממוהו יעוררו לתכלית ההתנשאות, ובמיעוט הביטול ימעיטו אור מדה זו כו'

blocks.text: The proof: the whole building of *hisnasus*, in length and breadth, depends only on the people's *bittul* (self-nullification). When they exalt him it is roused to the full; with less *bittul* it lessens. It comes *davka* from other people.

blocks.title: They praised Rashbi, and he said Torah
blocks.text: They came to *Rashbi* for rain and praised him, and he said Torah. *Davka* when people are *mevatel* (nullify) themselves to someone, it draws out the power of *Malchus*, for teaching too: it is when you know people are listening that you want to talk.

blocks.title: The listener falls asleep
blocks.text: You could say a person wants to talk anyway, that he wants to be *misnasei* (rise above) over other people. But if really nobody listens, he finally stops talking. If the listener falls asleep in the middle of the *shiur* (class), there is no one to talk to, and you say, "What am I talking for?" The same when nobody is really listening or cares.

blocks.title: The comedian with no audience
blocks.text: So with an actor on stage, a comedian: if everybody boos him, or even if they just don't respond, it is as though nobody cares. Take the extreme: he gets up and there is nobody in the audience at all. "So what am I going to do my act for?" Told he likes doing his act, so do it, he answers that he only likes to do it when there are people listening. That is the idea here.

phrases.he: אבל החסד כמו שהוא בעצם כך יתפשט,
phrases.en: The same way the *chesed* is *b'etzem*, that's how it'll spread out

phrases.he: וגם שיהיה בו ריבוי ומיעוט על פי אופן התעוררות המקבל אם הוא מבקש ברחמנות ביותר כו',
phrases.en: the guy's really asking with a big *rachmanus* on him, then there'll be more *chesed*

phrases.he: מכל מקום לא מזה יבא עיקר בנינה כו'
phrases.en: The main *binyan* will not come from that

phrases.he: ודי למבין.

blocks.text: But *chesed* spreads out the way it is in the self. It can be more or less by the receiver's arousal: **the guy's really asking with a big *rachmanus* on him, then there'll be more *chesed***. Still, **the main *binyan* will not come from that**: if he is not an *ish chesed*, there won't be *chesed*. The main building is already there.

sections.title: No king without a nation, yet hisnasus is in man from birth
sections.summary: As below, so above: there is no king without a people, and *hisnasus* is not drawn straight from the Essence. Yet it lies hidden in a person from birth, a baby wants to rule the animals, and it, not the intellect, is what sets man apart from the animals.

phrases.he: והנמשל מזה יש להבין למעלה, כי כמו מלכותא דארעא כך מלכותא דרקיע,
שאין מלך בלא עם דוקא
phrases.en: there is no king without a nation

phrases.he: והגם שההתנשאות דבחינת מדת מלכות למעלה הוא כשאר המדות העליונות,
אבל אינה המשכה ממש מבחינת העצמות

blocks.text: As the kingdom of earth, so the kingdom of heaven: **there is no king without a nation**. *Hisnasus* above is like the other upper *middos*, but it is not drawn *mamash* (actually) from the *Atzmus* (Essence): it comes *davka* from somebody else. In other places, though, it says just the opposite, that *Malchus* is rooted in the *etzem* (essence) more than the other *middos*.

phrases.he: (רק מכל מקום ישנה בכח ובהעלם גדול,
phrases.en: but nonetheless, really *b'koach v'helem gadol* it's there

phrases.he: כי בבחינת אדם גם בתינוק קטן,

יש בחינת ההתנשאות להתנשא על הכל, גם על הבהמה, שזהו בטבע תולדתו מיד, כמו שכתוב ורדו כו' כנראה בטבע התינוק, שתשוקתו למשול ולרדות על חיה ובהמה ועוף כו', כמו שכתוב במקום אחר שזהו דוקא מבחינת אדם, מה שאין כן מדת החסד והרחמים שישנה בבהמה גם כן, כנשר שהוא רחמני כו')

blocks.text: Still, it is there, in potential and great hiddenness: if it were not really there, it could not come out even through other people's *bittul*. **Even a little baby** has *hisnasus* over everything, even over the animals, by nature from birth, as it says, *u'rdu* ("and rule").

A baby's nature is to want to rule over beasts and birds. A person naturally has this attribute; what the text says is that its arousal, its *binyan*, comes *davka* from others. And it is only in man: *chesed* and mercy are in animals too, like the eagle, which is merciful. So the main difference between a person and an animal is not even the intellect, but *davka Malchus*.

sections.title: Over whom would G-d rule? He thought up somebody else, and made the tzimtzum for it
sections.summary: Rising above has delight only over another, and there is nothing besides G-d. So *Malchus* as a full *partzuf* needs His will that there be a separate something: for this there was the first *tzimtzum*, and for this *Malchus* is renewed every *Rosh Hashana*.

phrases.he: הגם שנקרא מדת ההתנשאות אבל עיקר בנינה הוא להתנשאות
על דרך זולתו,
ואז נמשך תענוג ורצון גדול בהתנשאות זו,
ולפי זה יש להבין איך יתכן למעלה באלקות, שאין לך דבר חוץ ממנו
phrases.en: So if that's how it is, how could it be such a thing upstairs?

phrases.he: על מי יתנשא כו'
phrases.en: who is He going to be *misnasei* on?

blocks.text: There are animals with all kinds of *middos*, but no animal really has an attribute of *Malchus*. They call the lion a king; it isn't really so. A lion is regal and very strong, but he is not trying to rule over anything. "He just wants to eat them."

Though it is called the attribute of *hisnasus*, its main building is to rise *davka* over somebody else, and then a great delight and will is drawn into it: rising above by oneself has no *taanug* (delight) and *ratzon* in it. **So if that's how it is, how could it be such a thing upstairs?** There is nothing besides Him; **who is He going to be *misnasei* on?**

phrases.he: ואם כן בחינת בנין המלכות ברצון ותענוג ומדות בבחינת פרצוף שלם בבחינת האצילות אי אפשר להיות,
כי אם כאשר עלה ברצונו שיהיה יש נפרד לעצמו, שיהיה על מי להתנשאות כו',
phrases.en: He had to think up of like there should be somebody else

phrases.he: אזי נתעורר אור מדה זו מן המאציל כו' ולזאת אמר יהו״ה מלך גאות לבש, שנתלבש במדה זו להיות מלך על עם ועל כן צריך דוקא למדה זאת לחדש אותה ממקור חוצבה בכל ראש השנה, דהיינו עד בחינת מחשבה בעצמות אור אין סוף, אנא אמלוך כו', בבחינת ההתנשאות שעלה בבחינת עצמותו עדיין קודם שהיה הצמצום כו'

blocks.text: So the building of *Malchus* as a full *partzuf* in *Atzilus*, with will, delight and *middos*, is impossible unless it arose in His will that there be a separate *yesh*, someone to rise over: **He had to think up of like there should be somebody else**. So *Malchus* is really rooted more in the *etzem*, to the point that He actually thought of having somebody else. That is *Hashem malach gei'us lavesh*: He dressed Himself in this attribute to be King of the world.

So this attribute has to be renewed every *Rosh Hashana*. It will not come up by itself; it needs the *bittul* of the *mekabel* (receiver) to renew it, all the way up to the thought in the Essence of the *Or Ein Sof*, *Ana Emloch*, the *hisnasus* that arose in His Essence before the *tzimtzum* (contraction).

phrases.he: ולזה היה הצמצום הראשון הנקרא מקום פנוי כו', כדי שיהיה דבר חוץ מן העצמות,
phrases.en: The whole reason why there's a *tzimtzum* is that there should be something outside the *Atzmus*

phrases.he: שיתכן על זה בחינת אור ההתנשאות דבחינת מלכות דאין סוף (וכמו שכתוב במקום אחר בענין גמלתהו טוב כו' בשרש העובדי כוכבים ומזלות, שהפרידן מאחדותו בבחינת החושך והצמצום כו', כדי שיהיה בחינת מדת התפארת,
שמדת התפארת גם כן אינו אלא בפני איש נכרי ומרוחק דוקא
phrases.en: to be *mispaer* on somebody, to be *shvitz*, what is to say, to show off against somebody is *davka* against somebody else

phrases.he: כו' ודי למבין)

blocks.text: That is why there was the first *tzimtzum*, called the *makom panui* (the empty place): **the whole reason why there's a *tzimtzum* is that there should be something outside the *Atzmus***, for the light of the *hisnasus* of *Malchus* of the *Ein Sof*.

*Gmalas'hu tov* is the opening of a *maamar* someplace. The text brings the root of the idol worshippers, separated from His unity in darkness and *tzimtzum* so that there be *tiferes* (glory), which is only before a stranger: to be *mispaer* (glorify oneself), to *shvitz* (boast), to show off, is *davka* against somebody else. *Malchus* is over your own guys; *tiferes* is *davka* over strangers, not your own nation. That is why He had to make other nations too.

sections.title: Malchus of Atzilus over the lower worlds: "I am first and I am last"
sections.summary: *Malchus* of *Atzilus* too is the will to rule over *Beriya, Yetzira and Asiya*, and needs the screen below *Atzilus* for it. *Malchus* is not an attribute of the self: unlike glory, victory or giving, which are only roused by another, it is built from the other.

phrases.he: וכך יובן בבחינת מלכות דאצילות, סופא דכל דרגין שבאצילות, שהוא רצון ותענוג כו' של מדת ההתנשאות להיות מלך על בי"ע, שלזה הוצרך להיות הצמצום דמסך שבין אצילות לבריאה,
phrases.en: This is the same way *inyan* of *Malchus* of *Atzilus*, to be *misnasei* over *Beriya, Yetzira and Asiya*, and for this you need a *masach* between *Atzilus* and *Beriya*

phrases.he: להיות ראש לשועלים כו'

blocks.text: *Malchus* of *Atzilus*, the end of all the levels of *Atzilus*, is the same: it is the will and delight **to be *misnasei* over *Beriya, Yetzira and Asiya***, and for this there had to be the *tzimtzum*, a *masach* between *Atzilus* and *Beriya*, "to be a head to the foxes".

phrases.he: והיינו אני ראשון בבחינת מלכות דאין סוף ואני אחרון במלכות דאצילות, כי נעוץ תחלתן בסופן, וזהו בכל ראש השנה וראש השנה כידוע ודי למבין

blocks.text: That is "I am first" in *Malchus* of the *Ein Sof* and "I am last" in *Malchus* of *Atzilus*: their beginning is wedged in their end, every *Rosh Hashana*. The *inyan* of *Malchus* is that it is not really a *sefira atzmis* (an attribute of the self). It has no existence without a *zulas* (another), and it is *davka* the arousal of the other that gives it its own; it is not roused from itself so much.

*Tiferes* is different: the other only gives it the ability to show off. The wish to *shvitz* is not built from the other guy; it is nice to have somebody to show off to, but being a *shvitzer* comes from himself. Wanting to be a king is *davka* over the other guy.

The same holds for the other *middos*, as he showed in *chesed*: *netzach* (victory) is *davka* to win over the other guy, *hod* is to make a *hod* on the other guy, *yesod* is to be *mashpia* (give) to the other guy. The intellect could even be just *atzmi* (of the self). The arousal of the *middos* has to do with somebody else, but their real *binyan* is not from another person.

blocks.title: Winning over a computer, or over yourself
blocks.text: Olympic athletes have their whole *taanug* *davka* in winning over other people: that is the *taanug* of *netzach*. But it doesn't have to be so: you can win over a computer, which is not really somebody else, or win over yourself. Mountain climbers take on a challenge themselves, though in a way the mountain is something else. But where somebody has to conquer eating or the like, that is *netzach mamash* over himself.

reviewQuestions.question: Why is Malchus called kalla, and what can speech carry that the other powers cannot?
How does hisnasus differ from chesed in where it comes from?
What do the sleeping listener and the comedian in an empty hall show about the proof from the people's bittul?
If hisnasus is built from others, how is it in a baby, and what does it show about man and the animals?
Why, according to this chapter, was there a first tzimtzum, and a masach between Atzilus and Beriya?

notes.text: Tape 227 words 0-1732 are not on chapter 48's lines: the class first finishes chapter 47's point that Malchus is a separate thing that can be copied (the computer, the Torah codes, Pac-Man), then goes over chapter 47 "real fast" (w1186-1732). The chapter 47 file does not cite tape 227, so these blocks are placed under line 1 with outOfPlace; a reviewer may prefer to move the recaps to chapter 47.

The Torah-codes digression answers an email from a listener (w593-627); the listener and the person who uploaded the seminars (named at w1029-1047) are left out. Saddam Hussein is named only as an example of what is encoded in the Torah, so the block is not flagged.

In the recap of chapter 47 he lists achor b'achor, achor b'panim and zanav but explains only the zanav, achor b'achor and a higher inner Malchus ("like the thing with the Name that's after and the Name that's before", w1358-1404, left out as unclear in the block).

Line 16: he says that in other places it says just the opposite, that Malchus is rooted more in the etzem than the other middos (w2747-2770); on line 20 (w3158-3191) he draws that conclusion himself. Both are kept as he says them.
Line 22: he reads "to renew it every month and every Rosh Hashana" (w3213-3224); the line has only every Rosh Hashana. The block follows the line.

Line 24: his remark that Malchus is over one's own people and tiferes over strangers, so He had to make other nations, explains the line's root of the idol worshippers; not flagged (the text's own claim). He calls Gmalas'hu tov "the beginning of a maamar someplace" without naming it.
The Rashbi story is told in one sentence (they came to him for rain, praised him, and he said Torah, w2281-2298); the block keeps it as he says it.

Phrase English: line 1's "because the Malchus has from all the sefiros in it" is his gloss of shekelula mehakol; line 20's "He had to think up... somebody else" (w3144-3157) is his gloss right after reading the line. Lines 2, 4-7, 9-11, 13, 21-22 and 26 are read without translation.
